BiblicalUsage: Yah is the shortened form of the LORD's name, Jehovah, sung when His people remember what He has done. Moses sang it at the Red Sea, calling the LORD his strength and song and salvation, and Isaiah takes up the same words to say that God is my salvation and I will trust and not be afraid. The name gathers up the whole story of deliverance into two syllables.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the shortest name of God carries the whole gospel: He is my strength, my song, and my salvation. When I have nothing left to say, I can still sing Yah, and it is enough.
RelatedEvents: The Exodus and the Red Sea
